q: 因为妈妈今天生病了，___我自己做晚饭。
zh: 因为妈妈今天生病了，所以我自己做晚饭。
py: yīn wèi mā ma jīn tiān shēng bìng le suǒ yǐ wǒ zì jǐ zuò wǎn fàn
en: Because Mum is ill today, I'm making dinner myself.
why: 因为 introduces the cause and 所以 introduces the result, in front of the second subject. 但是 would set up a contrast and 如果 a supposition, but this is a real reason.

q: ___我们家离学校很近，___我每天走路上学。
zh: 因为我们家离学校很近，所以我每天走路上学。
py: yīn wèi wǒ men jiā lí xué xiào hěn jìn suǒ yǐ wǒ měi tiān zǒu lù shàng xué
en: Because our home is close to school, I walk to school every day.
why: A real reason and its result: 因为 then 所以. 虽然…但是 would make the second clause a contrast, and 如果 or 只要 would turn the cause into a condition.

q: ___让女儿安静地学习，爸爸把电视关了。
zh: 为了让女儿安静地学习，爸爸把电视关了。
py: wèi le ràng nǚ ér ān jìng de xué xí bà ba bǎ diàn shì guān le
en: In order to let his daughter study in peace, Dad turned the TV off.
why: The first clause gives the goal Dad had in mind, so it takes 为了. 由于 and 既然 give a cause or known fact, and 如果 a supposition, none of which fit a purpose.

q: 既然这个手机已经坏了，我们___买一个新的吧。
zh: 既然这个手机已经坏了，我们就买一个新的吧。
py: jì rán zhè ge shǒu jī yǐ jīng huài le wǒ men jiù mǎi yī ge xīn de ba
en: Since this phone is already broken, let's buy a new one.
why: 既然 (since, given that) takes 就 after the second subject for a suggestion. 所以 and 可是 cannot follow 我们 here, and 才 would mean 'only then'.

q: 由于天气太冷，超市里的青菜卖得很贵，___很多人都不买。
zh: 由于天气太冷，超市里的青菜卖得很贵，因此很多人都不买。
py: yóu yú tiān qì tài lěng chāo shì lǐ de qīng cài mài de hěn guì yīn cǐ hěn duō rén dōu bù mǎi
en: Owing to the cold weather, greens are expensive in the supermarket, and therefore many people don't buy them.
why: The formal 由于 is answered by 因此 at the head of the result clause. 因为 would reverse cause and result, and 如果 or 虽然 would change the logic.

q: 既然你答应了孩子，你___应该带他去公园玩。
zh: 既然你答应了孩子，你就应该带他去公园玩。
py: jì rán nǐ dā ying le hái zi nǐ jiù yīng gāi dài tā qù gōng yuán wán
en: Since you promised the child, you should take him to the park.
why: 既然 leads to a conclusion with 就, and 就 stands after the subject 你. 所以, 可是 and 因此 are conjunctions and cannot sit between 你 and 应该.

q: ___这件衣服很便宜，___我不喜欢。
zh: 虽然这件衣服很便宜，但是我不喜欢。
py: suī rán zhè jiàn yī fu hěn pián yi dàn shì wǒ bù xǐ huan
en: Although this piece of clothing is cheap, I don't like it.
why: A real fact followed by an unexpected result takes 虽然…但是. 不但…而且 adds a second similar point, and 如果 or 只要 would make 便宜 a condition.

q: 虽然哥哥很忙，___他每天给奶奶打电话。
zh: 虽然哥哥很忙，但是他每天给奶奶打电话。
py: suī rán gē ge hěn máng dàn shì tā měi tiān gěi nǎi nai dǎ diàn huà
en: Although my brother is busy, he phones Grandma every day.
why: 虽然 needs 但是 in the second clause, in front of 他. 所以 would claim that being busy causes the calls, and 而且 and 然后 do not mark a contrast.

q: ___明天商店不打折，妈妈___会去买那双鞋。
zh: 即使明天商店不打折，妈妈也会去买那双鞋。
py: jí shǐ míng tiān shāng diàn bù dǎ zhé mā ma yě huì qù mǎi nà shuāng xié
en: Even if the shop has no sale tomorrow, Mum will still go and buy those shoes.
why: 明天 has not happened, so this is a supposed case: 即使…也. 虽然…但是 needs a fact that already exists, and 因为…所以 would state a cause.

q: 尽管鞋子很贵，奶奶___买给孙女了。
zh: 尽管鞋子很贵，奶奶还是买给孙女了。
py: jǐn guǎn xié zi hěn guì nǎi nai hái shi mǎi gěi sūn nǚ le
en: Even though the shoes were expensive, Grandma bought them for her granddaughter anyway.
why: 尽管 states a real fact and its partner is 还是 after the second subject. 才 and 就 do not express 'anyway', and 所以 would make the high price the reason for buying.

q: 就算你不说，爸爸___知道钱是你拿的。
zh: 就算你不说，爸爸也知道钱是你拿的。
py: jiù suàn nǐ bù shuō bà ba yě zhī dào qián shì nǐ ná de
en: Even if you don't say, Dad knows it was you who took the money.
why: 就算 (even if) takes 也 after the second subject. 但是 belongs with 虽然 and cannot follow 爸爸, and 才 or 所以 give the wrong logic.

q: ___家里已经有两台冰箱了，___妈妈还想再买一台。
zh: 虽然家里已经有两台冰箱了，但是妈妈还想再买一台。
py: suī rán jiā lǐ yǐ jīng yǒu liǎng tái bīng xiāng le dàn shì mā ma hái xiǎng zài mǎi yī tái
en: Although we already have two fridges at home, Mum still wants to buy another.
why: The two fridges are an existing fact that Mum ignores, so 虽然…但是. 只要, 如果 and 只有 all need a condition, and the second clause would not be a surprise.

q: 即使以后你搬到别的城市，爸爸妈妈___会常常给你打电话。
zh: 即使以后你搬到别的城市，爸爸妈妈也会常常给你打电话。
py: jí shǐ yǐ hòu nǐ bān dào bié de chéng shì bà ba mā ma yě huì cháng cháng gěi nǐ dǎ diàn huà
en: Even if you move to another city later, Mum and Dad will still call you often.
why: 即使 sets up a supposed future case and takes 也 after the second subject. 就 and 才 do not give 'still', and 却 needs a fact, not a supposition.

q: 只有你陪着，奶奶___愿意去医院。
zh: 只有你陪着，奶奶才愿意去医院。
py: zhǐ yǒu nǐ péi zhe nǎi nai cái yuàn yì qù yī yuàn
en: Grandma is only willing to go to the hospital if you go with her.
why: 只有 names the one condition that works, and its partner is 才. 就 belongs with 只要 and 如果.

q: 只要价格便宜，我___买。
zh: 只要价格便宜，我就买。
py: zhǐ yào jià gé pián yi wǒ jiù mǎi
en: As long as the price is cheap, I'll buy it.
why: 只要 (as long as) is paired with 就 after the second subject. 才 would turn the sentence into 'only if'.

q: 如果东西坏了，商店___给你换新的。
zh: 如果东西坏了，商店就会给你换新的。
py: rú guǒ dōng xi huài le shāng diàn jiù huì gěi nǐ huàn xīn de
en: If the item is broken, the shop will swap it for a new one.
why: 如果 takes 就 after the second subject 商店. 才会 would mean 'only then', and 所以 and 但是 cannot follow a subject.

q: ___你把作业写完，妈妈才让你看电视。
zh: 只有你把作业写完，妈妈才让你看电视。
py: zhǐ yǒu nǐ bǎ zuò yè xiě wán mā ma cái ràng nǐ kàn diàn shì
en: Only when you have finished your homework will Mum let you watch TV.
why: The 才 already in the sentence calls for 只有, the one condition that works. 只要 pairs with 就, and 虽然 or 既然 do not set a condition.

q: ___爸爸点头，妈妈就同意了。
zh: 只要爸爸点头，妈妈就同意了。
py: zhǐ yào bà ba diǎn tóu mā ma jiù tóng yì le
en: As long as Dad nodded, Mum agreed.
why: The 就 in the second clause points to 只要 (this one condition is enough). 只有 needs 才, and 虽然 or 即使 would not fit 就 here.

q: ___你能在六点前回家，我们___能一起去看电影。
zh: 只有你能在六点前回家，我们才能一起去看电影。
py: zhǐ yǒu nǐ néng zài liù diǎn qián huí jiā wǒ men cái néng yī qǐ qù kàn diàn yǐng
en: Only if you can be home before six can we go to the cinema together.
why: 'Only if' is 只有…才. 只要…就 would say that being home by six is enough, and the mixed pairs 只有…就 and 如果…才 do not exist.

q: 要是这家超市每天都打折的话，妈妈___会天天来买菜。
zh: 要是这家超市每天都打折的话，妈妈就会天天来买菜。
py: yào shi zhè jiā chāo shì měi tiān dōu dǎ zhé de huà mā ma jiù huì tiān tiān lái mǎi cài
en: If this supermarket had a sale every day, Mum would come to buy vegetables every day.
why: 要是…的话 takes 就 after the second subject. 才 belongs with 只有, and 可是 or 然后 cannot stand after 妈妈.

q: 除了爸爸，我们家的人___爱吃鱼。
zh: 除了爸爸，我们家的人都爱吃鱼。
py: chú le bà ba wǒ men jiā de rén dōu ài chī yú
en: Everyone in our family loves fish except Dad.
why: 'Except' is 除了…都. 还 would add to Dad, giving 'besides Dad, the others also...', which is not what is said here.

q: 不管价格___，姐姐都想买这条裙子。
zh: 不管价格贵不贵，姐姐都想买这条裙子。
py: bù guǎn jià gé guì bu guì jiě jie dōu xiǎng mǎi zhè tiáo qún zi
en: Whether the price is high or not, my sister wants to buy this skirt.
why: 不管 must be followed by an open question form, here the A-not-A 贵不贵. A plain statement such as 很贵 or 太贵 leaves nothing open.

q: 无论天气怎么样，爷爷每天早上___去公园。
zh: 无论天气怎么样，爷爷每天早上都去公园。
py: wú lùn tiān qì zěn me yàng yé ye měi tiān zǎo shang dōu qù gōng yuán
en: Whatever the weather is like, Grandpa goes to the park every morning.
why: 无论 plus an open question is answered by 都 after the second subject. 才 means 'only then', and 所以 cannot follow 每天早上.

q: 除了牛奶以外，妈妈___买了一些水果。
zh: 除了牛奶以外，妈妈还买了一些水果。
py: chú le niú nǎi yǐ wài mā ma hái mǎi le yī xiē shuǐ guǒ
en: Besides milk, Mum also bought some fruit.
why: 'Besides A, also B' is 除了…还. 都 would have to mean 'all except', which cannot work with a single purchase of 一些水果.

q: 除了星期天，这家商店每天___开门。
zh: 除了星期天，这家商店每天都开门。
py: chú le xīng qī tiān zhè jiā shāng diàn měi tiān dōu kāi mén
en: The shop is open every day except Sunday.
why: Sunday is left out, so the partner is 都 after 每天. 还 would mean 'in addition to Sunday', which makes no sense with 每天.

q: 不管是大人___孩子，在家里都要自己洗碗。
zh: 不管是大人还是孩子，在家里都要自己洗碗。
py: bù guǎn shì dà rén hái shi hái zi zài jiā lǐ dōu yào zì jǐ xǐ wǎn
en: Whether adults or children, everyone at home has to wash their own bowls.
why: 不管 needs the question form A 还是 B, which gives two open choices. 而且, 所以 and 然后 cannot link two alternatives.

q: 无论你想买___，妈妈都会先看看价格。
zh: 无论你想买什么，妈妈都会先看看价格。
py: wú lùn nǐ xiǎng mǎi shén me mā ma dōu huì xiān kàn kan jià gé
en: Whatever you want to buy, Mum will check the price first.
why: 无论 needs a question word. 什么 makes the object open; 东西, 一个 and 很多 are plain statements and cannot follow 无论.

q: 这家饭馆的菜___好吃___便宜。
zh: 这家饭馆的菜又好吃又便宜。
py: zhè jiā fàn guǎn de cài yòu hǎo chī yòu pián yi
en: The food in this restaurant is both tasty and cheap.
why: Two qualities of the same thing are joined by 又…又. 一边…一边 is for two actions happening at once.

q: 奶奶一边包饺子，___和孙子聊天。
zh: 奶奶一边包饺子，一边和孙子聊天。
py: nǎi nai yī biān bāo jiǎo zi yī biān hé sūn zi liáo tiān
en: Grandma chats with her grandson while making dumplings.
why: Two actions at the same time take 一边…一边, and the second 一边 stands right before the verb phrase. 又 would join qualities, and 先 or 才 would not mean 'at the same time'.

q: 这条裙子又___又好看。
zh: 这条裙子又便宜又好看。
py: zhè tiáo qún zi yòu pián yi yòu hǎo kàn
en: This skirt is both cheap and pretty.
why: Inside 又…又 the adjectives stay bare. 很, 太 or 非常 cannot be added between 又 and the adjective.

q: 妈妈既要上班，___要照顾孩子，每天都很累。
zh: 妈妈既要上班，又要照顾孩子，每天都很累。
py: mā ma jì yào shàng bān yòu yào zhào gù hái zi měi tiān dōu hěn lèi
en: Mum both has to work and look after the children, so she is tired every day.
why: 既 is matched with 又 (or 也) before the second verb phrase. 就, 才 and 而是 cannot complete 既.

q: 不但哥哥喜欢这个游戏，___弟弟也很喜欢。
zh: 不但哥哥喜欢这个游戏，而且弟弟也很喜欢。
py: bù dàn gē ge xǐ huan zhè ge yóu xì ér qiě dì di yě hěn xǐ huan
en: Not only my elder brother likes this game; my younger brother likes it a lot too.
why: The second clause has its own subject 弟弟, so the conjunction 而且 must stand in front of it. 还 is an adverb and cannot precede 弟弟.

q: 这件外套不但很便宜，___很暖和。
zh: 这件外套不但很便宜，还很暖和。
py: zhè jiàn wài tào bù dàn hěn pián yi hái hěn nuǎn huo
en: This coat is not only cheap, it is also very warm.
why: The shared subject 这件外套 is not repeated, so the adverb 还 opens the second part. 而是, 但是 and 所以 would change the meaning.

q: 他___是我的邻居，___是我最好的朋友。
zh: 他既是我的邻居，也是我最好的朋友。
py: tā jì shì wǒ de lín jū yě shì wǒ zuì hǎo de péng you
en: He is both my neighbour and my best friend.
why: 既…也 joins two identities of the same person. 一边…一边 is only for actions at the same time, and the others set up a condition or contrast.

q: 你先把钱付了，___拿东西。
zh: 你先把钱付了，再拿东西。
py: nǐ xiān bǎ qián fù le zài ná dōng xi
en: Pay first, then take the things.
why: 先…再 marks two steps in order. 都 and 也 do not mark a second step, and 所以 would make the first step a cause.

q: 爸爸一回家，我们___吃饭。
zh: 爸爸一回家，我们就吃饭。
py: bà ba yī huí jiā wǒ men jiù chī fàn
en: As soon as Dad gets home, we eat.
why: 一…就 means 'as soon as'. 才 would mean 'not until', and 再 or 又 do not pair with 一.

q: 他___下班就去超市买菜。
zh: 他一下班就去超市买菜。
py: tā yī xià bān jiù qù chāo shì mǎi cài
en: As soon as he finishes work he goes to the supermarket to buy food.
why: 一 goes before the first verb and is answered by 就. 先 or 再 do not combine with 就 to mean 'as soon as'.

q: 她___走进商店，___看见了那条红裙子。
zh: 她一走进商店，就看见了那条红裙子。
py: tā yī zǒu jìn shāng diàn jiù kàn jiàn le nà tiáo hóng qún zi
en: As soon as she walked into the shop, she saw that red dress.
why: 'As soon as' is 一…就. 先…再 would suggest she planned two steps, but seeing the dress is not a planned step.

q: 弟弟一看见玩具，___想让妈妈买。
zh: 弟弟一看见玩具，就想让妈妈买。
py: dì di yī kàn jiàn wán jù jiù xiǎng ràng mā ma mǎi
en: As soon as my little brother sees a toy, he wants Mum to buy it.
why: 一 + verb is always answered by 就 before the next verb. 才 would mean 'not until', and 再 or 也 do not fit.

q: 我们先去银行取钱，___去超市买东西。
zh: 我们先去银行取钱，然后去超市买东西。
py: wǒ men xiān qù yín háng qǔ qián rán hòu qù chāo shì mǎi dōng xi
en: We'll go to the bank to get money first, and then go shopping at the supermarket.
why: 先 opens the sequence and 然后 introduces the next step. 所以, 可是 and 因为 would give cause or contrast between the two trips.

q: 你先把衣服洗干净，___晾在外面。
zh: 你先把衣服洗干净，再晾在外面。
py: nǐ xiān bǎ yī fu xǐ gān jìng zài liàng zài wài miàn
en: First wash the clothes clean, then hang them outside.
why: 先 is followed by 再 for the second step. 还, 更 and 最 are degree or addition adverbs and do not mark a later step.

q: 天气越来越___了，我们去买厚衣服吧。
zh: 天气越来越冷了，我们去买厚衣服吧。
py: tiān qì yuè lái yuè lěng le wǒ men qù mǎi hòu yī fu ba
en: The weather is getting colder and colder; let's go and buy thick clothes.
why: 越来越 is followed by a bare adjective. 很, 太 and 非常 add a degree that 越来越 already expresses.

q: 这个孩子越长越___，已经比爸爸高了。
zh: 这个孩子越长越高，已经比爸爸高了。
py: zhè ge hái zi yuè zhǎng yuè gāo yǐ jīng bǐ bà ba gāo le
en: This child gets taller as he grows; he is already taller than his dad.
why: 越 + verb + 越 + adjective takes a bare adjective as the second part. 很, 更 and 太 cannot follow 越.

q: 这件衣服我___穿___喜欢。
zh: 这件衣服我越穿越喜欢。
py: zhè jiàn yī fu wǒ yuè chuān yuè xǐ huan
en: The more I wear this top, the more I like it.
why: The verb 穿 sits between the two parts, which is the 越…越 frame. 越来越 stands before one adjective or feeling verb and cannot surround a verb.

q: 雨___下___大，我们别去超市了。
zh: 雨越下越大，我们别去超市了。
py: yǔ yuè xià yuè dà wǒ men bié qù chāo shì le
en: The rain is getting heavier and heavier; let's not go to the supermarket.
why: The verb 下 stands between the two 越, giving 越下越大. 越来越 cannot be placed before the verb 下.

q: 妈妈做的菜越来越___，全家人都爱吃。
zh: 妈妈做的菜越来越好吃，全家人都爱吃。
py: mā ma zuò de cài yuè lái yuè hǎo chī quán jiā rén dōu ài chī
en: Mum's cooking is getting better and better and the whole family loves it.
why: 越来越 takes a bare adjective. 很, 非常 and 更 would double the degree, which is not allowed.

q: 你___着急，___容易出错，慢慢来吧。
zh: 你越着急，越容易出错，慢慢来吧。
py: nǐ yuè zháo jí yuè róng yì chū cuò màn màn lái ba
en: The more anxious you are, the easier it is to make mistakes; take it slowly.
why: Two linked changes, one growing with the other, are 越…越. 越来越 describes one thing changing over time, and 又…又 would only list two qualities.

q: 他买的不是苹果，___梨。
zh: 他买的不是苹果，而是梨。
py: tā mǎi de bù shì píng guǒ ér shì lí
en: What he bought was not apples but pears.
why: The sentence corrects A with B, so it is 不是…而是. 就是 would say it must be one of the two, and 要么 offers a choice.

q: 妈妈不是去超市买东西，___去银行取钱。
zh: 妈妈不是去超市买东西，而是去银行取钱。
py: mā ma bù shì qù chāo shì mǎi dōng xi ér shì qù yín háng qǔ qián
en: Mum isn't going to the supermarket to shop; she is going to the bank to get money.
why: A correction ('not A but B') takes 而是. 就是 would claim she always does one or the other, and 要么 offers options.

q: ___你自己去买，___让我去买，别再吵了。
zh: 要么你自己去买，要么让我去买，别再吵了。
py: yào me nǐ zì jǐ qù mǎi yào me ràng wǒ qù mǎi bié zài chǎo le
en: Either you go and buy it yourself or let me go; stop arguing.
why: Two options to choose between are 要么…要么. 不是…而是 would be a correction, and 不但…而且 an addition.

q: 周末弟弟不是在家看电视，___在房间玩游戏，从来不出门。
zh: 周末弟弟不是在家看电视，就是在房间玩游戏，从来不出门。
py: zhōu mò dì di bù shì zài jiā kàn diàn shì jiù shì zài fáng jiān wán yóu xì cóng lái bù chū mén
en: At weekends my brother is always either watching TV at home or playing games in his room; he never goes out.
why: 'Always one or the other' is 不是…就是. 而是 would correct a claim ('not A but B'), which does not fit the habitual cue.

q: 既然你不想去，___自己去了。
zh: 既然你不想去，我就自己去了。
py: jì rán nǐ bù xiǎng qù wǒ jiù zì jǐ qù le
en: Since you don't want to go, I'll go by myself.
why: 就 is an adverb and goes after the second subject: 我就. 就我 puts it in front of the subject, which is never correct.

q: 虽然这个钱包很旧，___还很好用。
zh: 虽然这个钱包很旧，但是它还很好用。
py: suī rán zhè ge qián bāo hěn jiù dàn shì tā hái hěn hǎo yòng
en: Although this wallet is old, it is still very useful.
why: 但是 is a conjunction and stands before the second subject: 但是它. After the subject it would be wrong, and 所以 or 因此 give the wrong logic.

q: 不管天气怎么样，___去市场买菜。
zh: 不管天气怎么样，奶奶都去市场买菜。
py: bù guǎn tiān qì zěn me yàng nǎi nai dōu qù shì chǎng mǎi cài
en: Whatever the weather, Grandma goes to the market to buy food.
why: The partner of 不管 is 都, and it follows the subject: 奶奶都去. 都奶奶 is out of order, and 才 or 就 do not pair with 不管.

q: 只有你同意，___能买这台洗衣机。
zh: 只有你同意，我们才能买这台洗衣机。
py: zhǐ yǒu nǐ tóng yì wǒ men cái néng mǎi zhè tái xǐ yī jī
en: We can buy this washing machine only if you agree.
why: 只有 takes 才, and 才 sits after the second subject: 我们才. 才我们 and 就我们 put the adverb before the subject, and 就 does not go with 只有.

zh: 如果孩子不想去，我们就不去了。
py: rú guǒ hái zi bù xiǎng qù wǒ men jiù bù qù le
en: If the child doesn't want to go, we won't go.
why: 就 is an adverb and follows the second subject 我们. 如果 may stand before or after 孩子.

zh: 只有你亲自去，他才会同意。
py: zhǐ yǒu nǐ qīn zì qù tā cái huì tóng yì
en: Only if you go in person will he agree.
why: 只有 is answered by 才, which comes after the second subject 他 and before the verb. 就 would be the wrong partner.

zh: 因为下雨，所以我们没去超市。
py: yīn wèi xià yǔ suǒ yǐ wǒ men méi qù chāo shì
en: Because it rained, we didn't go to the supermarket.
why: 因为 opens the reason clause and 所以 opens the result clause, in front of the subject 我们.

zh: 虽然这个包很贵，但是妈妈还是买了。
py: suī rán zhè ge bāo hěn guì dàn shì mā ma hái shi mǎi le
en: Although this bag is expensive, Mum bought it anyway.
why: 但是 comes before the second subject 妈妈, while 还是 comes after it. 虽然 may precede or follow 这个包.

zh: 除了爷爷，我们都喜欢吃鱼。
py: chú le yé ye wǒ men dōu xǐ huan chī yú
en: All of us like fish except Grandpa.
why: 'Except' pairs 除了 with 都, and 都 comes after 我们. 除了爷爷 may also follow 我们.

zh: 这件衣服又便宜又好看。
py: zhè jiàn yī fu yòu pián yi yòu hǎo kàn
en: This piece of clothing is both cheap and good-looking.
why: 又…又 joins two qualities, each 又 directly before its adjective, with no 很. The two adjectives can swap places.

zh: 他一下班就去买菜。
py: tā yī xià bān jiù qù mǎi cài
en: He goes to buy groceries as soon as he finishes work.
why: 一 comes right before the first verb 下班 and 就 right before the second verb. Neither can come before the subject.

zh: 你先把鞋脱了，再进房间。
py: nǐ xiān bǎ xié tuō le zài jìn fáng jiān
en: Take your shoes off first, then go into the room.
why: 先 marks the first step and 再 the next, both after the subject and before their verb phrases.

zh: 天气越来越冷了。
py: tiān qì yuè lái yuè lěng le
en: The weather is getting colder and colder.
why: 越来越 goes directly before the adjective. 很 would be wrong here and is left out.

zh: 妈妈越说，孩子越不听。
py: mā ma yuè shuō hái zi yuè bù tīng
en: The more Mum talks, the less the child listens.
why: In 越…越 each 越 sits directly before its verb, one in each clause, each after its own subject.

zh: 他不是我的哥哥，而是我的表哥。
py: tā bù shì wǒ de gē ge ér shì wǒ de biǎo gē
en: He is not my brother but my cousin.
why: A correction is 不是 A 而是 B, with 而是 right in front of the corrected part.

zh: 周末妈妈不是逛街，就是在家做饭。
py: zhōu mò mā ma bù shì guàng jiē jiù shì zài jiā zuò fàn
en: At weekends Mum is always either out shopping or cooking at home.
why: 不是 A 就是 B says it is always one of the two. The time word 周末 can come before or after 妈妈.

zh: 只要价格合适，我们就买。
py: zhǐ yào jià gé hé shì wǒ men jiù mǎi
en: As long as the price is right, we'll buy it.
why: 就 is an adverb that follows the second subject 我们. 只要 may come before or after 价格.

zh: 不管价格高不高，爸爸都要买这台冰箱。
py: bù guǎn jià gé gāo bu gāo bà ba dōu yào mǎi zhè tái bīng xiāng
en: Whether the price is high or not, Dad wants to buy this fridge.
why: 不管 needs an A-not-A question (高不高) and 都 after the subject 爸爸. 爸爸 may also open the sentence.

zh: 除了水果，妈妈还买了牛奶。
py: chú le shuǐ guǒ mā ma hái mǎi le niú nǎi
en: Besides fruit, Mum also bought milk.
why: 'Besides A, also B' is 除了…还, with 还 after the subject. 除了水果 may also follow 妈妈.

zh: 不但弟弟爱玩游戏，而且妹妹也爱玩。
py: bù dàn dì di ài wán yóu xì ér qiě mèi mei yě ài wán
en: Not only does my younger brother love playing games, my younger sister loves it too.
why: The clauses have different subjects, so 不但 comes before the first subject and 而且 before the second.

zh: 姐姐一边做饭一边听音乐。
py: jiě jie yī biān zuò fàn yī biān tīng yīn yuè
en: My elder sister listens to music while she cooks.
why: 一边…一边 puts each 一边 directly before its verb, with the subject first.

zh: 为了让孩子吃得健康，妈妈每天都自己做饭。
py: wèi le ràng hái zi chī de jiàn kāng mā ma měi tiān dōu zì jǐ zuò fàn
en: So that her child eats healthily, Mum cooks for herself every day.
why: 为了 opens the goal clause. 都 follows 每天 and comes before the verb phrase. 每天 may come before or after 妈妈.

zh: 既然你不舒服，就别去上班了。
py: jì rán nǐ bù shū fu jiù bié qù shàng bān le
en: Since you're not feeling well, don't go to work.
why: 既然 leads to a suggestion with 就, which stands directly before the verb phrase. 既然 may come before or after 你.

zh: 即使明天商店不打折，我也要去。
py: jí shǐ míng tiān shāng diàn bù dǎ zhé wǒ yě yào qù
en: Even if the shop has no sale tomorrow, I'm going.
why: 即使 sets up the supposed case and 也 follows the second subject 我. 我 may also precede 即使.

src: 大家都喜欢吃辣，爷爷不喜欢。
src_py: dà jiā dōu xǐ huan chī là yé ye bù xǐ huan
zh: 除了爷爷，大家都喜欢吃辣。
py: chú le yé ye dà jiā dōu xǐ huan chī là
en: Everyone likes spicy food except Grandpa.
why: 'Everyone except Grandpa' is 除了 A, with 都 after the subject 大家. The phrase 除了爷爷 can also follow 大家.

src_py: mā ma huí jiā hòu mǎ shàng zuò fàn
zh: 妈妈一回家就做饭。
py: mā ma yī huí jiā jiù zuò fàn
en: Mum cooks as soon as she gets home.
why: 一 goes right before the first verb 回家 and 就 right before 做饭, both after the subject.

src: 只要你付钱，他就给你这个东西。
src_py: zhǐ yào nǐ fù qián tā jiù gěi nǐ zhè ge dōng xi
task: Make payment the only condition: use 只有…才.
zh: 只有你付钱，他才给你这个东西。
py: zhǐ yǒu nǐ fù qián tā cái gěi nǐ zhè ge dōng xi
en: He will give you this thing only if you pay.
why: 只有 marks the only condition that works, so its partner is 才 instead of 就, after the second subject 他.

src: 这个手机很好用，也很便宜。
src_py: zhè ge shǒu jī hěn hǎo yòng yě hěn pián yi
task: Join the two points with 不但…而且.
zh: 这个手机不但很好用，而且很便宜。
py: zhè ge shǒu jī bù dàn hěn hǎo yòng ér qiě hěn pián yi
en: This phone is not only easy to use, it is also cheap.
why: The subject is shared, so it comes before 不但, and 而且 then introduces the second quality.

src: 我去买鞋，没有去买衣服。
src_py: wǒ qù mǎi xié méi yǒu qù mǎi yī fu
task: Say 'not A but B' with 不是…而是.
zh: 我不是去买衣服，而是去买鞋。
py: wǒ bù shì qù mǎi yī fu ér shì qù mǎi xié
en: I'm not going to buy clothes; I'm going to buy shoes.
why: A correction is 不是 A 而是 B. 就是 would claim it is always one of the two.

s: 如果东西坏了，就商店给你换新的。
s_py: rú guǒ dōng xi huài le jiù shāng diàn gěi nǐ huàn xīn de
zh: 如果东西坏了，商店就给你换新的。
py: rú guǒ dōng xi huài le shāng diàn jiù gěi nǐ huàn xīn de
en: If it is broken, the shop will swap it for a new one.
why: 就 is an adverb and must follow the second subject 商店, not stand in front of it.

s: 只有你同意，我们就买这台电视。
s_py: zhǐ yǒu nǐ tóng yì wǒ men jiù mǎi zhè tái diàn shì
zh: 只有你同意，我们才买这台电视。
py: zhǐ yǒu nǐ tóng yì wǒ men cái mǎi zhè tái diàn shì
en: We'll buy this TV only if you agree.
why: 只有 (the only condition) goes with 才. 就 belongs to 只要 and 如果.

s: 不管价格很贵，妈妈都要买。
s_py: bù guǎn jià gé hěn guì mā ma dōu yào mǎi
zh: 不管价格多贵，妈妈都要买。
py: bù guǎn jià gé duō guì mā ma dōu yào mǎi
en: However expensive the price is, Mum will buy it.
why: 不管 needs an open question form such as 多贵. 很贵 is a plain statement and cannot follow it.

s: 因为让孩子高兴，爸爸给他买了新玩具。
s_py: yīn wèi ràng hái zi gāo xìng bà ba gěi tā mǎi le xīn wán jù
zh: 为了让孩子高兴，爸爸给他买了新玩具。
py: wèi le ràng hái zi gāo xìng bà ba gěi tā mǎi le xīn wán jù
en: To make the child happy, Dad bought him a new toy.
why: Making the child happy is the aim of the purchase, so the opener must be 为了. 因为 would need a reason that already exists.

s: 就算价格很高，但是爸爸也要买。
s_py: jiù suàn jià gé hěn gāo dàn shì bà ba yě yào mǎi
zh: 就算价格很高，爸爸也要买。
py: jiù suàn jià gé hěn gāo bà ba yě yào mǎi
en: Even if the price is high, Dad will still buy it.
why: 就算 pairs with 也 after the subject and cannot take 但是, which belongs with 虽然.

s: 这条裤子一边便宜一边好看。
s_py: zhè tiáo kù zi yī biān pián yi yī biān hǎo kàn
zh: 这条裤子又便宜又好看。
py: zhè tiáo kù zi yòu pián yi yòu hǎo kàn
en: These trousers are both cheap and nice-looking.
why: 一边…一边 joins two actions done at once. Qualities of one thing are joined by 又…又.

s: 一妈妈回家，我们就吃饭。
s_py: yī mā ma huí jiā wǒ men jiù chī fàn
zh: 妈妈一回家，我们就吃饭。
py: mā ma yī huí jiā wǒ men jiù chī fàn
en: As soon as Mum gets home, we eat.
why: 一 must stand right before the first verb, after the subject 妈妈, not at the very start of the clause.

s: 超市里的人越来越很多了。
s_py: chāo shì lǐ de rén yuè lái yuè hěn duō le
zh: 超市里的人越来越多了。
py: chāo shì lǐ de rén yuè lái yuè duō le
en: There are more and more people in the supermarket.
why: 越来越 already expresses degree, so 很 cannot follow it.

s: 这不是我的钱包，但是我妹妹的。
s_py: zhè bù shì wǒ de qián bāo dàn shì wǒ mèi mei de
zh: 这不是我的钱包，而是我妹妹的。
py: zhè bù shì wǒ de qián bāo ér shì wǒ mèi mei de
en: This is not my wallet but my younger sister's.
why: 'Not A but B' is 不是…而是. 但是 follows 虽然 and cannot complete 不是.

s: 除了星期一，这家商店每天还开门。
s_py: chú le xīng qī yī zhè jiā shāng diàn měi tiān hái kāi mén
zh: 除了星期一，这家商店每天都开门。
py: chú le xīng qī yī zhè jiā shāng diàn měi tiān dōu kāi mén
en: The shop is open every day except Monday.
why: Monday is left out, so the partner is 都. 还 means 'besides', which does not fit 每天.

s: 只要你喜欢，就我买给你。
s_py: zhǐ yào nǐ xǐ huan jiù wǒ mǎi gěi nǐ
zh: 只要你喜欢，我就买给你。
py: zhǐ yào nǐ xǐ huan wǒ jiù mǎi gěi nǐ
en: As long as you like it, I'll buy it for you.
why: 就 is an adverb and follows the subject 我. Placed before 我 it is wrong.

s: 因为太累了，我所以早睡了。
s_py: yīn wèi tài lèi le wǒ suǒ yǐ zǎo shuì le
zh: 因为太累了，所以我早睡了。
py: yīn wèi tài lèi le suǒ yǐ wǒ zǎo shuì le
en: Because I was too tired, I went to bed early.
why: 所以 is a conjunction and must stand in front of the subject 我, not after it.

s: 因为超市今天打折，所以人特别多。
zh: 因为超市今天打折，所以人特别多。
py: yīn wèi chāo shì jīn tiān dǎ zhé suǒ yǐ rén tè bié duō
en: Because the supermarket has a sale today, there are a lot of people.
why: Using both 因为 and 所以 is normal Chinese, unlike English. 所以 sits at the head of the result clause.

s: 虽然哥哥已经吃饱了，但是他还是想吃蛋糕。
zh: 虽然哥哥已经吃饱了，但是他还是想吃蛋糕。
py: suī rán gē ge yǐ jīng chī bǎo le dàn shì tā hái shi xiǎng chī dàn gāo
en: Although my brother is already full, he still wants to eat cake.
why: 虽然 keeps its partner 但是, even though English drops 'but'. 还是 follows the subject 他.

s: 要是价格不太高的话，姐姐就买。
zh: 要是价格不太高的话，姐姐就买。
py: yào shi jià gé bù tài gāo de huà jiě jie jiù mǎi
en: If the price isn't too high, my sister will buy it.
why: 要是 and 的话 may frame the if-clause together, and 就 follows the second subject 姐姐.

s: 除了周末以外，爸爸每天都加班。
zh: 除了周末以外，爸爸每天都加班。
py: chú le zhōu mò yǐ wài bà ba měi tiān dōu jiā bān
en: Dad works overtime every day except at weekends.
why: 'Except' takes 都 after the subject, and 以外 is optional but allowed.

s: 不管是大的还是小的，妹妹都喜欢。
zh: 不管是大的还是小的，妹妹都喜欢。
py: bù guǎn shì dà de hái shi xiǎo de mèi mei dōu xǐ huan
en: My younger sister likes them whether big or small.
why: A 还是 choice is a valid open question after 不管, and 都 follows the subject 妹妹.

s: 弟弟一回家就要看电视。
zh: 弟弟一回家就要看电视。
py: dì di yī huí jiā jiù yào kàn diàn shì
en: As soon as my little brother gets home, he wants to watch TV.
why: Here 一 and 就 share one subject, so the subject appears only once, before 一.

s: 孩子们越玩越开心，一直不想回家。
zh: 孩子们越玩越开心，一直不想回家。
py: hái zi men yuè wán yuè kāi xīn yī zhí bù xiǎng huí jiā
en: The more the children play, the happier they get, and they don't want to go home.
why: 越 + verb + 越 + adjective is correct when one thing grows with another, and the adjective is bare.

s: 要么你来我家，要么我去你家，我们得见一面。
zh: 要么你来我家，要么我去你家，我们得见一面。
py: yào me nǐ lái wǒ jiā yào me wǒ qù nǐ jiā wǒ men děi jiàn yī miàn
en: Either you come to my place or I go to yours; we have to meet.
why: 要么…要么 offers two options to choose from, and each 要么 opens its clause before the subject.
